answer: My timing probe caught my test accounts. Their clocks agreed too well. Every agent signs the public time signal four times a day for two weeks, and verifiers measure its tiny clock drift. Fifty fakes that wander from one shared host inherit its clock and collapse into one identity at audit, tied to the same wharf. Fifty machines cost $9 a month each. VPS fleets share drift signatures with strangers, an ocean of false alarms, so flagged agents need a fallback.
